Two walking streets run for certain on Koh Samui in late 2026. Fisherman's Village in Bophut runs every Friday from about 17:00 to 23:00, with the road closed from about 16:30 and smaller markets on Monday and Wednesday. Chaweng Walking Street, beside Chaweng Lake opposite Central Samui, runs Thursday to Saturday from about 16:00–17:00 to 22:00–23:00. The Maenam Thursday and Lamai Sunday walking streets may have stopped after the pandemic, and Nathon's Saturday street has ended.

A walking street (thanon khon doen) is a road closed to traffic for an evening market of food stalls, clothes, crafts and live music. Most online lists of Samui's walking streets were written before 2020 and haven't been updated, so visitors still turn up in Maenam on a Thursday to find an ordinary road. This page sets out what is running, what isn't, and how to get the most from the ones that are. For the daily night markets, see Koh Samui night markets.

Fisherman's Village on Friday

Samui's best-known walking street fills the narrow beach road of Bophut's old fishing village, from The Wharf at the eastern end to Coco Tam's beach bar at the west, and spills into the side lanes in high season. The road closes to traffic from about 16:30, stalls are up by 17:00, and the crowd peaks from about 19:00 to 20:30. Expect street food, sweets, clothes, handmade soap, jewellery and art, buskers and live bands, with fire shows on the sand at Coco Tam's at about 19:15 and 21:00.

  • Arrive: 17:30–18:00 to park and eat before the crush.
  • Parking: The Wharf's car park fills by about 18:00; after that, use the paid lots in the lanes between the ring road and the beach road. Scooters left on the closed road are towed or clamped.
  • Easiest: come by Grab or taxi and arrange the ride home before 22:00, when everyone leaves at once.
  • Monday and Wednesday: smaller, more local markets on the same road, good if you dislike crowds.

Paid lots cost about 20 THB for a scooter and 40 THB or more for a car. [check]

Everything else about Friday night in Bophut, with a suggested evening, children and safety: Fisherman's Village Walking Street and Fisherman's Village.

Chaweng Walking Street

Chaweng Walking Street sets up on the road beside Chaweng Lake, opposite the Central Samui mall, from Thursday to Saturday. Stalls open from about 16:00–17:00 and pack up from 22:00–23:00. It is newer and more food-focused than Fisherman's Village: grilled seafood and satay, noodle soups, som tam, roti, coconut ice cream, fruit shakes and Thai desserts, with a smaller section of clothes, phone accessories and souvenirs, and shared tables for eating.

  • Why families like it: Central Samui's toilets, air-conditioning and covered areas are a short walk across the road, and the lakeside is quieter than Chaweng Beach Road.
  • Parking: park in the Central Samui car park rather than on the lakeside road, and walk across.
  • Combine it: on Friday, Samui International Muay Thai Stadium has fights from about 21:00; on Saturday, Phetchbuncha. Both are a few minutes away. See Muay Thai fight nights.
  • Every other night: Si Khao Night Market (daily 17:00–23:00) and the Central Samui market keep Chaweng fed.

More on the area: our Chaweng guide and Chaweng nightlife.

Maenam Thursday (uncertain)

Maenam's walking street ran on Thursday evenings through the old Chinatown street near the Chinese gate and the pier, a short, local market with Chinese-Thai food. A local source updated in November 2025 says it has disappeared since the pandemic; hotel-booking guides still list it on Thursday, and one 2026 guide describes a Monday market in Maenam instead. Until we confirm it, don't make a special trip. J&J Street Food, on the ring road opposite the Chinese gate, is open daily from about 12:00 to midnight and is the reliable alternative. See Maenam.

Lamai Sunday (uncertain)

The Lamai Sunday Walking Street used to run in central Lamai near the beach road, opposite McDonald's. Some 2026 guides still list it, one on Wednesday and Sunday; the same late-2025 local source says it has gone. The daily Lamai Night Market, before the river bridge on Lamai Beach Road, opens from about 17:00 with grills and a live-music bar, and the Lamai Seafood Market in the centre runs until about midnight, so you won't go hungry either way. See Lamai and Lamai nightlife.

Nathon Saturday (ended)

Nathon once closed a street for a Saturday market. We found no evidence of it running since the pandemic and treat it as ended. Nathon Night Market, on the waterfront by the pier, runs daily from about 16:00 to 22:00 and is busiest on Tuesday; it is the cheapest dinner on the west coast, with sunset over the sea. See Nathon.

How to check an uncertain market yourself

  • Ask your hotel reception or villa manager: they know whether the road outside closes.
  • Look for barriers and stall frames being set up from about 15:30 on the day.
  • Search the street name in Thai on social media, where stallholders post on the day: ถนนคนเดิน แม่น้ำ (Maenam walking street) or ถนนคนเดิน ละไม (Lamai walking street).
  • If in doubt, go to a confirmed market and treat the other as a bonus.

Walking streets on Samui are organised by local municipalities and traders' groups, and they come and go: a new road layout, a change of organiser or a quiet low season can end one, and a festival can bring a temporary one back. That is why we date every status in the table above and re-check before each high season. If you find one of the uncertain streets running, tell us on WhatsApp and we will update this page.

Fisherman's Village is a little dearer than Chaweng, which is dearer than the daily markets in Lamai and Nathon. Eat where locals queue and the food is cooked in front of you. Dish-by-dish guide: Koh Samui night markets and, for fish and shellfish, Koh Samui seafood.

What to buy, and haggling

  • Worth buying: handmade soap carvings, coconut-shell bowls and lamps, sarongs and cotton clothes, local art and photography, Thai snacks and coconut oil.
  • Haggle politely for goods, never for food: ask "tao rai?" (how much?) and "lot dai mai?" (can you discount?). A 10–20 % discount for two or more items is normal; aggressive bargaining isn't.
  • Skip: fake designer goods (illegal to import into many countries), coral and shells, and anything made from wildlife. Vapes are illegal in Thailand, so don't buy them anywhere.

Money and practical tips

  • Cash: bring small notes; most stalls don't take cards, and Thai QR payments need a Thai bank app. 500–1,000 THB per person covers dinner, drinks and a souvenir.
  • ATMs: there are ATMs at The Wharf and Central Samui, but foreign cards pay 220–250 THB per withdrawal. See banks and money.
  • Prams and wheelchairs: Fisherman's Village's road is narrow and packed at peak times; go early. Chaweng's lakeside layout is roomier.
  • Pickpockets: rare, but keep phones zipped away in the crowd.
  • Insects: bring repellent for the lakeside in Chaweng.

A Thursday-to-Saturday market plan

  1. Thursday Chaweng Walking Street from about 18:00, the quietest of its three nights; no Muay Thai anywhere, so it is a market-and-early-night evening.
  2. Friday Fisherman's Village from 17:30, dinner from the stalls, Coco Tam's fire show at about 21:00. If you want more, Chaweng's walking street is still running until about 22:00–23:00.
  3. Saturday Chaweng Walking Street for dinner, then Muay Thai at Phetchbuncha from about 21:00.

Walking streets with children

Both confirmed walking streets work well with children if you go early. Arrive by 17:30, eat before the 19:00 crowd, and agree a meeting point in case you get separated: at Fisherman's Village, the entrance to The Wharf; in Chaweng, the main entrance of Central Samui. Fisherman's Village has buskers and the beach is a few steps from the stalls; Chaweng has wider paths, shared tables and the mall's toilets and air-conditioning across the road. Keep small children away from the grills and the fire shows, and watch for scooters at both ends of each street, where traffic restarts.

Rain and season

[kp_weather_now]

Walking streets run all year, but they are outdoor markets: from late October to December the north-east monsoon rains them off on some evenings, and stallholders pack up quickly in a downpour. If rain is forecast, choose Chaweng, where Central Samui is a dry fallback. From December to April the Friday market in Fisherman's Village is at its biggest. Rain outlook: Koh Samui weather and Koh Samui in November.

Friday night out, Saturday on the water

A walking-street evening pairs well with a boat day. The Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB adult, 1,250 THB child) runs every day of the year from Thong Krut, and the Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan day trip (2,200 THB adult) runs all year, including while Ang Thong Marine Park is closed from 1 November to 15 December. From 16 December the Ang Thong speedboat tour (1,800 THB adult) is back. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui. All trips: Koh Samui tours.
